page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock of 3.2 GHz. The instance provisions 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 105 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5000 MHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2045.0 and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 33.24 GB/sec, placing it within the upper 25 percent of measured hardware. Multi-threaded performance sits within the middle 50 percent, reflecting a Geekbench multi-core score of 12124.0 and PassMark CPU score of 24806.62. Because this instance utilizes a burstable CPU allocation profile within the Flex tier, it balances hardware resource costs against sustained full-core compute, making sustained maximum utilization less deterministic than dedicated c7i equivalents.

The c7i-flex.4xlarge instance is technically suited for batch processing, build automation, CI/CD test runners, distributed web serving, and CPU-focused applications that leverage modern instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX without requiring continuous 100 percent core saturation or high-speed local disk caches.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring an Intel Xeon 8488C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. It offers 16 vCPUs over 8 physical cores and 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5000 MHz, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The configuration includes no onboard local storage, zero dedicated GPUs, and a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates upper-quartile results in single-threaded performance, achieving 33.24 GB/sec in gzip compression and a 2045.0 Geekbench single-core score, alongside average multi-core and memory subsystem metrics. Utilizing burstable compute credits, c7i-flex.4xlarge delivers a cost-efficient balance for intermittent compute bursts rather than non-stop peak loads. It is engineered for workloads such as build automation, CI/CD pipelines, static web serving fleets, and general compute-bound enterprise applications that do not require attached local NVMe drives.
